UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
ALEXANDRIA DIVISION

MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE, Plaintiff, v. KATIE HALL, individually; NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN; META PLATFORMS, INC.; and JOHN/JANE DOES 1–6, Defendants. ____________________________________/ | Case No. 1:26-cv-02331

[PROPOSED] INTERIM ORDER SETTING ABBREVIATED SUBMISSIONS ON PLAINTIFF’S ADMINISTRATIVE MOTION

Plaintiff’s Administrative Motion for Expedited Briefing, Priority Determination, and a Defined Decision Schedule for the Two Rule 26(d)(1) Applications (ECF No. [___]) (the “Administrative Motion”) is before the Court. The Court will receive abbreviated submissions on the schedule and routing requested before ruling. It is hereby ORDERED:

1.	Opposition and reply dates. The dates in this paragraph provide two business days after notice of this Order for opposition and one business day after the opposition deadline for reply. A business day is a day that is not a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday as defined in Rule 6(a)(6), and the day of the triggering event is excluded. Any opposition to the schedule and routing requested in the Administrative Motion must be filed and served by [date]. Plaintiff may file and serve one reply by [date]. These are fixed calendar deadlines. No additional days attach to those dates because of the method of service. Each party filing an opposition or reply under this Order shall also send a contemporaneous electronic courtesy copy to each other party, in addition to service under Rule 5; Plaintiff’s address for that purpose is jayballentine@protonmail.com. Courtesy delivery does not constitute consent to electronic service and starts no period.

2.	Submission. The Administrative Motion becomes submitted after its opposition deadline has passed and Plaintiff has filed and served the authorized reply or the reply deadline has passed. If no opposition is filed, the Administrative Motion becomes submitted when its opposition deadline passes. An opposition by one party does not close another party’s opposition period, and an early reply does not close any party’s opposition period. The Administrative Motion will be determined on the papers, without a hearing, immediately after it becomes submitted.

3.	Scope. This Order concerns the timing, submission, and routing of the two Applications identified in the Administrative Motion. It does not concern the merits of any discovery request and grants no discovery. It changes no briefing deadline that governs either Application unless and until a further order does so. No deadline imposed by this Order operates retroactively. No further motion is required to obtain the Court’s ruling on the schedule and routing requested in the Administrative Motion.

Alexandria, Virginia

__________, 2026
